subject: Concurrency & rate limits follow-up (SLOs + quota request)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>, Bob Patel <bob.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: concurrency, latency SLOs, next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today 4 great conversation. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can scope the pilot and quota request:

- SLO targets you mentioned: 95th percentile latency <= 100ms for short-chat lookups; 99th percentile target for long streaming responses around 800ms (streaming tail).
- Expected throughput: steady-state 200 requests/sec (rps) with 3x burst to 600 rps during peak feed ingestion windows.
- Concurrency/connection model: your app will hold ~1.5k long-lived websocket connections for streaming and 500 parallel HTTP short requests per region. You indicated you use a connection pool on your side (Node-based pool with keep-alive).
- Important for us: whether you need token-level rate limits (tokens/minute) versus request-level concurrency caps, and whether you need reserved concurrency for Dedicated to guarantee throughput.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll run this against our performance playground to validate p95/p99 at the 200 rps / 500 parallel short request point and a streaming test with 1.5k connections.
2) We’ll produce a short mutual action plan (MAP) with test scenarios and success criteria.
3) I’ll request an elevated quota/temporary rate-limit bump for the pilot while we validate.

Attached: initial concurrency/rate-limit matrix (redwood_concurrency_limits_v2.pdf).

Are there any corrections to the numbers above? If not, I’ll schedule the perf run for next week and loop in our infra lead.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Bob Patel <bob.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: concurrency, latency SLOs, next steps

Thanks Marissa  that all looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 1.5k long-lived connections are for event streams where each connection streams multiple messages; average message size is ~2KB, but spikes to 50KB.
- For short requests, the 500 parallel requests is per region; we expect to run in us-east and us-west initially.
- We prefer request-level concurrency caps combined with a soft tokens/minute quota for burst protection.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood guarantee a soft isolated concurrency pool for us during pilot (e.g., 750 reserved concurrent slots) to avoid noisy neighbor issues?
2) What is the expected throttling behavior  immediate 429s, or token-bucket smoothing with Retry-After headers?

If you can answer those, we’ll finalize the MAP and share our internal traffic replay for the perf run.

Bob Patel
VP, Engineering  Platform, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Bob Patel <bob.patel@acme.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: concurrency, latency SLOs, next steps

Great questions  answers below and proposed pilot plan.

1) Reserved concurrency/pools: Yes  for Dedicated customers we can allocate reserved concurrency pools. For Hosted we can provision a temporary elevated pool for pilot customers; for your pilot we can offer a 750 reserved concurrent slot allocation for a 2-week window while we validate (subject to legal/ops approval).

2) Throttling behavior: Our hosted tier uses a hybrid approach: request-level concurrency caps (hard) and a token-bucket smoothing layer. Under transient bursts we apply token-bucket smoothing and surface Retry-After. If the burst exceeds reserved limits persistently, requests will receive 429 with standard Retry-After. For streaming connections, we monitor active streams separately and prioritize p95 tail for active connections.

3) Streaming: We support both SSE and WebSocket streams. We recommend using connection pooling with keep-alive and multiplexing where possible. For large messages (~50KB spikes) we suggest enabling chunked streaming on your side to keep per-frame latency low.

Pilot plan (high level):
- Day 03: Baseline perf run using your traffic replay (we’ll run in our perf sandbox, us-west).
- Day 47: Increase concurrency to 750 reserved slots; validate p95/p99 and streaming tails.
- Day 814: Pilot production mirror with gradual ramp and monitoring (observability hooks + tracing).

Deliverables: perf report, MAP doc, temporary quota bump (tokens/minute and reserved concurrency), and suggested rollback policy.

I’ve attached the concurrency/rate-limit matrix and included an initial quota proposal inline:
- Default hosted quota: 100k tokens/minute / 200 concurrent short requests.
- Pilot proposal: 500k tokens/minute / 750 reserved concurrent slots (2-week window).
- Post-pilot: move to Dedicated reserved capacity or negotiated hosted commit.

Next steps: if this aligns, I’ll ask Ops to open the temporary quota and share the HubSpot MAP link. Also looping in Logan to confirm infra capacity for the perf run.

Marissa

(Attachment: redwood_concurrency_limits_v2.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme pilot quota request / pricing note

Laura/Logan  quick internal note on Acme pilot:

- Acme is asking for a 2-week pilot with 750 reserved concurrent slots and 500k tokens/minute for validation. They have a strong chance to convert to a Dedicated commit if results are good.
- Financial ask: anticipate a short-term credit + pilot infrastructure allocation. I recommend approving the temporary quota and limited credit (33% ARR equivalent) under standard pilot terms.
- Can you confirm ops can provision the reserved pool in us-west for 14 days starting 2027-06-21? Also need a thumbs-up on the temporary credit approval so I can include in the MAP.

Thanks  Marissa

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
